title: Psalms Chapter 91 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 91 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 91 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 91.

questions.question: What shall he that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High abide under?
questions.explanation: The verse states that he shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty (Psalms 91:1).

questions.question: According to Psalms 91, what does the psalmist call the LORD?
questions.explanation: The psalmist refers to the LORD as his refuge and fortress (Psalms 91:2).

questions.question: What will the LORD deliver thee from, according to Psalms 91?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler (Psalms 91:3).

questions.question: Under what shall we trust according to Psalms 91?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that his truth shall be thy shield and buckler (Psalms 91:4).

questions.question: Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night or what?
options: The arrow that flieth by day
questions.correctAnswer: The arrow that flieth by day
questions.explanation: The verse mentions not being afraid for the arrow that flieth by day (Psalms 91:5).

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist says that there will be no destruction that wasteth at noonday.
questions.explanation: The verse refers to the pestilence that walketh in darkness and the destruction that wasteth at noonday, indicating that such destruction is acknowledged (Psalms 91:6).

questions.question: What will happen to a thousand at thy side and ten thousand at thy right hand?
options: It shall not come nigh thee
questions.correctAnswer: It shall not come nigh thee
questions.explanation: The verse assures that while a thousand shall fall at thy side, it shall not come nigh thee (Psalms 91:7).

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist will see the reward of the wicked with his eyes.
questions.explanation: The verse states that only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked (Psalms 91:8).

questions.question: What does the psalmist make the LORD in Psalms 91?
questions.explanation: The psalmist makes the LORD his habitation (Psalms 91:9).

questions.question: True or False: No evil shall befall thee according to Psalms 91.
questions.explanation: The verse states that there shall no evil befall thee (Psalms 91:10).

questions.question: According to Psalms 91, who shall keep thee in all thy ways?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that he shall give his angels charge over thee (Psalms 91:11).

questions.question: What shall the angels do, as stated in Psalms 91?
options: Lift thee up in their hands
questions.correctAnswer: Lift thee up in their hands
questions.explanation: The verse states that they shall bear thee up in their hands (Psalms 91:12).

questions.question: What shall the psalmist trample under feet?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that thou shalt tread upon the lion and adder (Psalms 91:13).

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist states that he will not deliver those who do not know his name.
questions.explanation: The psalmist indicates that he will deliver those who have set their love upon him and known his name (Psalms 91:14).

questions.question: In what circumstance will the psalmist call upon the LORD?
questions.explanation: The verse states that he shall call upon me, and I will be with him in trouble (Psalms 91:15).

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 91 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 91 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 91:7, what is the fate of those around you compared to your own protection?
options: Thousands will fall near you, but harm will not reach you
You will fall with many others around you
Only a few will be protected while many perish
Everyone will be equally protected including you
questions.correctAnswer: Thousands will fall near you, but harm will not reach you
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:7 states that a thousand may fall at your side and ten thousand at your right hand, but harm will not come near you, emphasizing God's special protection.

questions.question: What will you see with your eyes according to Psalms 91:8?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says you will behold with your eyes and see the reward of the wicked, indicating awareness of justice from a place of safety (Psalms 91:7-8).

questions.question: How does Psalms 91:9 describe the effect of making the LORD your refuge?
options: You become immune to all troubles
You will live in a city of peace
questions.explanation: Verse 9 teaches that when you make the LORD your refuge, He becomes your habitation, symbolizing intimacy and security (Psalms 91:9-10).

questions.question: What promise is given in Psalms 91:10 about evil and plague?
options: No evil or plague shall come near your dwelling
Evil will come but plague will not
Only a plague will be kept away
Evil and plague will test your faith
questions.correctAnswer: No evil or plague shall come near your dwelling
questions.explanation: Verse 10 clearly states that no evil will befall you and no plague will come near your home, emphasizing divine protection (Psalms 91:9-10).

questions.question: According to Psalms 91:11, what role do angels have concerning the believer?
options: They are charged to keep you in all your ways
They fight your battles for you
They give you strength to overcome sin
They teach you wisdom and understanding
questions.correctAnswer: They are charged to keep you in all your ways
questions.explanation: Verse 11 states that God will command His angels to guard and protect you in every way, showing God's care through angelic ministry (Psalms 91:11-12).

questions.question: What specific protection do the angels provide as described in Psalms 91:12?
options: They will bear you up so you won't hurt your foot
They will shield you from arrows
They will fight lions and dragons for you
They will give you wings to fly away
questions.correctAnswer: They will bear you up so you won't hurt your foot
questions.explanation: Verse 12 explains that angels will lift you up in their hands to prevent you from injuring yourself, demonstrating God's protective care (Psalms 91:11-12).

questions.question: How does Psalms 91:7-8 teach us about faith when surrounded by danger?
options: It encourages trust that God protects even when others fall
It warns believers to avoid danger at all costs
It suggests that believers will never see evil around them
It states that believers must fight to survive
questions.correctAnswer: It encourages trust that God protects even when others fall
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 highlight that even if many fall, the believer remains unharmed and witnesses the consequences of wickedness, teaching trust and confidence in God's protection.

questions.question: What does Psalms 91:9-10 imply will happen if you make the LORD your refuge?
options: No evil or plague will come near your home
You will be immune to all hardships
You will be wealthy and honored
You will never face any trial
questions.correctAnswer: No evil or plague will come near your home
questions.explanation: These verses connect making God your refuge with divine protection from evil and plague, emphasizing the safety found in trusting Him (Psalms 91:9-10).

questions.question: A believer is afraid of unseen dangers at night. According to Psalms 91, what truth should encourage them?
options: God’s angels are given charge to protect in all ways
Fear is a sign of weak faith
Night dangers are stronger than day dangers
You must stay awake to guard yourself
questions.correctAnswer: God’s angels are given charge to protect in all ways
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:11 promises that God commands His angels to guard believers in all their ways, offering reassurance against fears including those at night.

questions.question: What lesson about humility and trust can be drawn from the promise in Psalms 91:12?
options: Trusting God allows one to be lifted above harmful circumstances
One should rely solely on personal strength
Avoid all risks to prevent harm
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting God allows one to be lifted above harmful circumstances
questions.explanation: Verse 12 teaches that angels bear you up to prevent harm, symbolizing how humble trust in God elevates and protects believers (Psalms 91:11-12).

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 91:8 assures that the believer will be unaware of the wicked’s punishment.
questions.explanation: Verse 8 states the believer will see the reward of the wicked, meaning they are aware of their just punishment, not unaware.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 91:10, making the LORD your refuge guarantees no evil or plague will come near your dwelling.
questions.explanation: Verse 10 clearly promises that no evil or plague will come near when the LORD is made your refuge, affirming divine protection.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 91:7 emphasizes that the believer will face the same dangers and outcome as those around them.
questions.explanation: Verse 7 contrasts the believer's protection with the many who fall around them, showing the believer is uniquely kept safe.

questions.question: What does Psalms 91:11-12 teach about God's care in daily life?
options: God’s angels actively guard and support believers to avoid harm
Believers must rely on their own wisdom to avoid danger
Protection comes only during spiritual conflicts
God’s care is symbolic and not practical
questions.correctAnswer: God’s angels actively guard and support believers to avoid harm
questions.explanation: These verses describe angels given charge over believers to keep them safe and prevent injury, illustrating God’s active care in everyday life.

questions.question: How does Psalms 91:9-12 collectively encourage a believer facing trials?
options: By assuring refuge in God and angelic protection against all dangers
By instructing to isolate oneself from others
By promising wealth and earthly success
By saying that trials indicate lost faith
questions.correctAnswer: By assuring refuge in God and angelic protection against all dangers
questions.explanation: Verses 9-12 emphasize making God your refuge and the angels’ protection, offering comfort and strength during trials.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 91 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 91.

questions.question: According to Psalms 91:13, which creatures are mentioned as being trampled underfoot?
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:13 specifically states that one shall tread upon the lion and adder, the young lion and the dragon shall be trampled under feet.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Psalms 91:14 for God delivering and setting on high the person who trusts Him?
options: Because he hath set his love upon God and known His name
Because he has great wealth and power
Because he is righteous and perfect
Because he has many followers and priests
questions.correctAnswer: Because he hath set his love upon God and known His name
questions.explanation: The verse states that God will deliver and exalt the person because he has set his love upon Him and has known His name, indicating intimacy and trust.

questions.question: What promise does God make about His response when the faithful call upon Him, as stated in Psalms 91:15?
options: He will answer, be with them in trouble, deliver and honour them
He will delay His answer until they prove worthy
He will provide riches and fame
He will only answer in times of peace
questions.correctAnswer: He will answer, be with them in trouble, deliver and honour them
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:15 promises that God will answer when called upon, will be with the person in trouble, deliver them, and honour them.

questions.question: In Psalms 91:16, what does God say He will provide to the faithful?
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states that God will satisfy with long life and show His salvation to the person who trusts Him.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is thematically connected to the promise of divine protection in Psalms 91:11-12, where angels are charged to keep and bear up the faithful?
questions.explanation: Psalm 34:7 speaks of the angel of the LORD encamping around those who fear Him and delivering them, paralleling Psalms 91:11-12's promise of angelic protection.

questions.question: The imagery of God's protection 'under his wings' in Psalms 91:4 echoes which Old Testament symbol of God's refuge?
options: Ruth 2:12 - 'May he be like a winged eagle over his house'
Deuteronomy 32:11 - 'As an eagle stirreth up her nest'
Exodus 19:4 - 'I bare you on eagles' wings'
Psalm 36:7 - 'How excellent is thy lovingkindness, O God!'
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 19:4 - 'I bare you on eagles' wings'
questions.explanation: The metaphor of being under God's wings in Psalms 91:4 is reminiscent of Exodus 19:4, where God describes carrying Israel on eagles’ wings, symbolizing protection and care.

questions.question: In Psalms 91:13, the mention of 'dragon' is best understood as referring to what in the ancient Near Eastern context?
options: A mythical sea monster symbolizing chaos
A literal reptile common in Palestine
A metaphor for the Babylonian king
questions.correctAnswer: A mythical sea monster symbolizing chaos
questions.explanation: The 'dragon' (Hebrew 'tannin') often symbolizes chaos monsters in ancient Near Eastern literature, representing forces of evil or chaos defeated by God.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 91:7-8 when describing the fall of thousands around the faithful but their own safety?
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 use synonymous parallelism to contrast the fate of many falling around the person with the person's safety, a common Hebrew poetic device.

questions.question: What Hebrew word translated as 'refuge' in Psalms 91:2 and 9 also conveys the idea of a 'stronghold' or 'fortress'?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Machseh' means refuge or stronghold, emphasizing God as a place of safety and protection as in Psalms 91:2 and 9.

questions.question: According to Psalms 91:15, what relationship does God promise to have with those who call upon Him?
questions.explanation: The verse promises God will answer those who call on Him and be with them in trouble, showing an active, caring relationship.

questions.question: Psalms 91:16's promise of 'long life' contradicts the New Testament teaching on eternal life.
questions.explanation: While Psalms 91:16 promises long life and salvation, the New Testament expands this to eternal life through Christ (John 3:16), showing continuity rather than contradiction.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of divine protection and angelic ministry found in Psalms 91:11-12?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 1:14 describes angels as ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation, echoing the guardian role of angels in Psalms 91:11-12.

questions.question: How does the promise in Psalms 91:10 about no evil or plague befalling the faithful relate to the Exodus narrative in the Old Testament?
options: It parallels God’s protection of Israel during the plagues in Egypt
It contradicts Israel’s experience in the wilderness
It refers to a future messianic kingdom only
It is unrelated to the Exodus story
questions.correctAnswer: It parallels God’s protection of Israel during the plagues in Egypt
questions.explanation: The promise echoes God’s protection over Israel in Exodus 12 where the plague passed over their homes, symbolizing divine safeguarding.

questions.question: The phrase 'He shall cover thee with his feathers' in Psalms 91:4 is an example of which literary device?
questions.explanation: The phrase metaphorically depicts God’s protection as a bird sheltering its young, symbolizing care and safety.

questions.question: Which New Testament figure is often associated typologically with the protection and refuge themes in Psalms 91, especially verses 9-11?
questions.explanation: Jesus is often seen as the ultimate refuge and protector, fulfilling the protective promises of God in Psalms 91, as in Matthew 4:6 where Satan quotes this Psalm.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 91 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 91 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 91:1 teach about the nature of God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:1 describes God as the 'Most High' and emphasizes His protection, indicating that He is a refuge and fortress for those who dwell in Him.

questions.question: In Psalms 91:3, what is God said to deliver us from?
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:3 specifically states that God shall deliver thee from 'the snare of the fowler,' illustrating His protective nature against traps and dangers.

questions.question: What attribute of God is emphasized in Psalms 91:4 when it mentions 'His truth'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:4 highlights God's truth as a shield, which points to His faithfulness to protect and uphold His promises.

questions.question: What does Psalms 91:10 promise regarding evil?
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:10 assures that 'no evil shall befall thee,' emphasizing God's protective promise for those who trust in Him.

questions.question: What is indicated in Psalms 91:14 about those who love the Lord?
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:14 states that because of love for the Lord, He promises to deliver those who trust in Him, showcasing His commitment to His faithful.

questions.question: Which of the following does Psalms 91:11 say God provides?
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:11 notes that God gives His angels charge over us, indicating divine protection and care in all our ways.

questions.question: What does Psalms 91:12 indicate about the protection provided by angels?
options: They will lead us to prosperity
They will keep us from harm
questions.correctAnswer: They will keep us from harm
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:12 clarifies that angels will bear us up, ensuring we do not dash our foot against a stone, highlighting God's protective measures.

questions.question: According to Psalms 91:7, what assurance is given about the fate of the wicked?
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:7 states that a thousand shall fall at your side, indicating the ultimate downfall of the wicked while God's people remain unharmed.

questions.question: How does Psalms 91:5 describe the believer's response to fear?
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:5 reassures believers that they shall not be afraid of terror by night or arrows by day, emphasizing security in God.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 5-6 and verse 11 convey about God's protection?
options: God's angels protect us from danger
questions.correctAnswer: God's angels protect us from danger
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 indicate that believers need not fear dangers, while verse 11 affirms that God sends angels to safeguard them in their paths.

questions.question: What does Psalms 91:6 warn against?
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:6 mentions a warning against the destruction that wasteth at noonday, indicating the pervasive dangers that can threaten even in broad daylight.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'long life' in Psalms 91:16 imply about God's promises?
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:16 promises 'long life' to those who trust in God, which reflects His blessing upon their days in this earthly existence.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not protect believers from harm. What does Psalms 91:9-10 actually teach?
options: God does not care for believers
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:9-10 shows that God's protection is tied to making Him a refuge; thus, it is conditional upon one's relationship with Him.

questions.question: What insight does Psalms 91:15 provide about God's relationship with the believer in times of trouble?
questions.explanation: Psalms 91:15 assures that God will be with the believer in trouble and will answer them, indicating His active presence and support.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can be drawn from the phrase 'shadow of the Almighty' in Psalms 91:1?
questions.explanation: The 'shadow of the Almighty' in Psalms 91:1 signifies the protective and comforting presence of God over those who seek refuge in Him.
